questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to go to Australia. Of the available possible partner universities I found UWA to be the most intriguing one due to its location in Perth. I was intrigued by the remoteness of Perth (it is the world's most isolated metropole) and the city's access to beautiful beaches as well as the close by Rottnest Island ("Rotto").

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been one of the most transforming experience of my life. I have learned so much about the world and thereby also about myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UWA was very good at informing and guiding exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses, guided walks, emailed information etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was good.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really easy! There is a large street running right next to the University called College Row. Along the street there are five colleges. I lived at Trinity Residential College, which was a great place with nice people and a strong community. Ultimately, most of my friends from my exchange were from college, not university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's good...?

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied. No complaints. Would recommend.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To be honest, I do not remember it all that well. I remember that I had to supply information on courses passed at my home university. Then based on this information it was assessed whether or not I was allowed to study a given course at my host university. I remember the assessment being quite strict with several of my requested courses being denied.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The information in the application portal.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As said, somewhat unsuccessful. But I did expect rejection on some of them though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You're allowed to apply for a total of 8 courses. I will recommend that you apply for all 8 courses in case some of your requests are denied.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: See below.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I study comparative literature at UCPH and hence did English courses at UWA. The overall academic level was lower at UWA with discussions being less theoretical than what I was used to. I did not mind this at all, however.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I much preferred the teaching style of UWA. Lectures were 1 hour, tutorials were 1,5 hours compared to 2 and 3 hours respectively at UCPH. Furthermore student assessment was based partially on classroom participation which made sure that most of the class was engaged compared to UCPH where assessment is not based on classroom participation wherefore there will often only be a couple of students actively participating at the seminar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UWA had many clubs. They only allow participation before a certain deadline, so be observant.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had everything and all sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you're into.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore as much of Perth and Western Australia and the Rest of Australia as possible. It is a magnificent place!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Australians, and people from Perth in particular, are easygoing, pragmatic, and have a good sense of humor.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them about sports. They love their sports in Australia. In Western Australia they prefer footy (AFL) to rugby (NRL).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I know its a controversial thing to say but sometimes I did not feel comfortable around the indigenous (aboriginal) population. I had some bad encounters with people trying to pick a fight. But I did also meet some really nice, funny, and passionate aboriginal people, so I don't want to generalize.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beach-culture. Australians is a coastal people like the Danes. They love their beaches, their surfing, their swimming, their boating, their sunrises and sunsets. It's very endearing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. In Perth, they are very strict with alcohol
2. If you want to see the South Western Australia (Margaret River, Albany, Esperance etc.) make sure to go during the Australian summer, when the weather is good (October - March), cause you can always see the Northern parts of Australia during the Australian winter.
3. Check out Rottnest Island.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Get a "Transperth" Card as soon as possible - it's basically a rejsekort for Perth.
Get the Uber app.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing the country and forming friendships with people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing really...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go for it, you're gonna love it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
